400436.title: Yang Jun: Two of Us
400436.overview: Yang Jun, a young Daegu artist, paints a girl called Hana and her companion Duri, an octopus imagined as a gentle, intelligent creature rather than a monster. Together they dive into the deep sea, fly and travel, a pairing of two very different beings that stands for understanding and coexistence between people and nature, and between people of different backgrounds.

400594.title: Lee Daecheon: The Language of Landscape
400594.overview: Lee Daecheon studied painting in Korea and in Dresden and Berlin, and has worked in Germany for more than twenty years. Starting from East Asian landscape painting, he combines the spirit of traditional Korean painting with a contemporary visual language in what he calls ‘drawing the world’: layered landscapes where abstraction and figuration, memory and reality overlap. They depict no particular place, but a world of constantly changing connections that each viewer reads through their own memories.

400437.title: Goo Gijeong: Clearview Mechanism
400437.overview: The first Gana Art solo show by Goo Gijeong (b. 1990), who uses photography, graphics, video and installation to make familiar natural scenes strange through technology. Twelve works expose the conditions behind an image: a transparent steel frame showing the LED boards and renderings that make a picture, real plants set beside their digital renderings, and landscapes re-photographed and transformed again and again until they drift far from the original. A thoughtful show about how what we see as reality is made.
